atoms.text: After World War II, Rosie the Riveter became an important icon of the United States’ women’s movement. The iconic image already called for feelings of strength and patriotism during the war. These feelings accompanied women in their fight for the so-called Equal Rights Amendment or E.R.A.

hint.text: Rosie the Riveter is a cultural icon in the United States who represents the women who worked in factories and shipyards during World War II

atoms.text: The E.R.A. was already introduced in 1923 after women in the United States were given the right to vote, but was not passed by the Senate until 1972. The E.R.A. basically stated that gender should not influence the legal rights of men or women. Furthermore, it was drafted to work against forms of discrimination against women in different states. Although many were for the amendment, there were plenty of E.R.A. critics too.

atoms.a: What did Rosie the Riveter stand for after the World War?
b: ++ A symbol of strength for the women’s movement.
A symbol for the strength of men.
For the strong muscles women got after working.

atoms.a: What is the author’s main reason for writing the text?
b: ++ To generally explain what the E.R.A. was and what it stood for.
To show that there were many E.R.A. critics.
To show the development of the women’s rights movement all over the world.

atoms.a: What evidence does the author mention to support their text?
b: ++ The first drafting of the E.R.A. and the amendment’s content.
The amount of discrimination women and men experienced.
The development of the women’s rights movement all over the world.
